title: Incorporating AI in foreign language education: An investigation into ChatGPT’s effect on foreign language learners
extended_summary:
This paper investigates how ChatGPT affects foreign language learning experiences and how students perceive its strengths, challenges, and possible uses in language education. The authors position the study as addressing a gap in understanding the practical classroom use of generative AI, especially ChatGPT, in foreign language instruction. The research questions focus on how ChatGPT shapes learners’ experiences, motivation, engagement, and skill development, and what students see as the tool’s benefits, drawbacks, and recommendations for improvement.

The intervention was a four-week ChatGPT-integrated English course conducted online. ChatGPT was embedded into reading, writing, grammar, and vocabulary lessons, each 45 minutes long, using tailored lesson plans based on coursebook units. Students used the tool for activities such as warm-ups, pre-reading exploration, vocabulary practice, creative writing, grammar practice, brainstorming, story generation, social media simulation, and receiving writing feedback. The teacher initially provided prompts, then encouraged students to generate their own prompts in later weeks to support greater independence and creativity.

The study involved 13 preparatory-class university students at a School of Foreign Languages at a foundation university in Ankara, Turkey. Participants were 18–20 years old, came from multiple academic departments, and had English proficiency levels ranging from A2 to B2. Because of a post-earthquake shift to emergency distance education, both the instructional activities and the semi-structured interviews were conducted online. Data were collected through interviews and analyzed thematically within a qualitative case study framework.

The main conclusions are that students generally perceived ChatGPT as beneficial for writing, grammar, and vocabulary learning, and as increasing motivation and engagement through immediate feedback, accessibility, and versatility. Students also reported value for creativity and cultural exploration. At the same time, they noted limited usefulness for speaking and no impact on listening, plus concerns about overreliance, technical issues, misuse, and weak responsiveness to emotional or highly personal communication. The authors conclude that ChatGPT can be a useful supplementary tool in foreign language education but should complement rather than replace teacher guidance and authentic communicative practice.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed qualitative case study with a clear methodology, intervention description, and thematic analysis, but it lacks a control group, causal identification, and objective outcome measures. It meets limited credibility criteria and is therefore best classified as yellow.
impact_tier_rationale: Reported impacts are generally positive but based on small-sample self-reports without effect sizes or independent assessments, making magnitude unclear. In addition, the study is outside K-12 and thus offers only limited evidence for the school-age literacy review context.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT was integrated into online foreign-language instruction over four weeks for reading, writing, grammar, and vocabulary activities, including brainstorming, question answering, story generation, role-play creation, research proposal ideation, and teacher-provided or student-generated prompting.

ChatGPT was used specifically as a language-learning and writing support tool to help students draft essays, brainstorm ideas, practice grammar, expand vocabulary, and receive written feedback on essays in EFL instruction.

finding.finding_summary: In this qualitative case study, students reported that ChatGPT positively supported writing improvement, vocabulary learning, and some reading/writing classroom tasks during a four-week intervention. Evidence comes from interview themes rather than standardized literacy assessments; no effect sizes or comparative statistics were reported, and the study involved 13 university EFL preparatory students rather than K-12 learners.
finding.measure: Semi-structured interview reports on writing improvement, vocabulary learning, reading/writing activity experiences

finding.finding_summary: Students perceived benefits for grammar-related language development, but speaking improvement was reported as limited and listening improvement as absent. These findings are based on participant perceptions from interviews after four weeks of ChatGPT-assisted online EFL activities, with no direct fluency test scores or effect sizes reported.
finding.measure: Semi-structured interview reports on grammar, speaking, and listening impacts

finding.finding_summary: Most participants described increased motivation and engagement from ChatGPT's interactive, accessible, and versatile use in online classes, though a few reported no increase in motivation. Findings are qualitative and perception-based, derived from interviews with 13 learners after a four-week implementation; no validated motivation scale or effect size was reported.
finding.measure: Semi-structured interview reports on motivation and engagement

finding.finding_summary: Students reported that ChatGPT supported creativity, brainstorming, and interactive learning activities, but also raised concerns about overreliance, shortcut-taking, and possible weakening of autonomy or critical thinking. These conclusions are based on thematic analysis of interview data rather than direct performance measures.
finding.measure: Semi-structured interview reports on creativity, interactivity, dependency, and shortcut-taking

finding.finding_summary: Participants reported that ChatGPT saved time and made information access and research tasks more efficient during language-learning activities. However, these efficiency findings were self-reported qualitatively and were not quantified with task-time or productivity metrics.
finding.measure: Semi-structured interview reports on time-saving and efficiency
